title: Lexcura Clinical Insights
author: michellec9547
description:
Lexcura Clinical Insights is a podcast for attorneys and legal professionals handling complex healthcare litigation.

Hosted by Michelle Carroll, Founder and Chief Clinical Strategist of Lexcura Summit, each episode examines how clinical records, regulatory standards, timelines, care plans, staffing data, assessment tools, and causation evidence can be used to identify negligence, strengthen liability theories, evaluate damages, and improve case strategy.

The podcast explores litigation involving hospitals, nursing homes, long-term care facilities, and home health agencies. Topics include failure to rescue, sepsis, medication errors, falls, pressure injuries, hospital-acquired infections, scope-of-practice violations, missed visits, staffing failures, regulatory breaches, diagnostic delay, readmissions, and other preventable adverse outcomes.

Episodes also address the practical business of healthcare litigation, including case screening, intake strategy, chronology development, expert preparation, portfolio management, pre-discovery investigation, mediation leverage, case valuation, and building authority in specialized areas of medical negligence.

Lexcura Clinical Insights helps attorneys move beyond simply reading medical records to understanding what the records reveal, what may be missing, how the evidence connects, and how clinical intelligence can support stronger and better-informed litigation decisions.

title: The Political Campaign Podcast: Running for Office, Campaign Strategy, Candidates, Campaign Managers, Fundraising, GOTV, Messaging, Field Operations, Debates and Winning Elections
author: Podily
description:
The Political Campaign Podcast explores the strategy, organization, messaging, fundraising, and field operations behind running for office and winning elections. Designed for candidates, campaign managers, political consultants, staffers, volunteers, activists, and anyone interested in how modern campaigns actually work, the show examines the decisions that shape campaigns from the first exploratory conversations through Election Day. Episodes cover campaign planning, candidate positioning, voter targeting, opposition research, endorsements, media strategy, debate preparation, polling, fundraising, budgeting, staffing, compliance, digital advertising, and the day-to-day realities of building a competitive political operation.

The podcast also dives deep into voter contact and turnout strategy, including GOTV, canvassing, phone banking, texting, direct mail, volunteer recruitment, field offices, voter registration, data analytics, persuasion, coalition building, grassroots organizing, earned media, social media, campaign events, rapid response, crisis communications, and election-night operations. Episodes examine how campaigns use voter files, polling, demographics, fundraising data, geographic targeting, message testing, and political technology to identify supporters, persuade undecided voters, allocate resources, and maximize turnout. The show also looks at the roles played by campaign managers, communications directors, finance teams, field organizers, consultants, pollsters, media buyers, political parties, PACs, donors, volunteers, and outside organizations.

From city council and school board races to mayoral, legislative, congressional, gubernatorial, and presidential campaigns, The Political Campaign Podcast examines what candidates and campaign teams need to understand before asking voters for their support. Topics include deciding whether to run, building a campaign team, developing a winning message, raising money, managing a candidate’s schedule, navigating political attacks, preparing for debates, communicating with the press, organizing supporters, complying with election rules, surviving the final weeks of a race, and learning from both successful and unsuccessful campaigns. Whether you are considering running for office, working on a campaign, studying political strategy, or simply fascinated by elections, the podcast provides an in-depth look at the people, systems, tactics, and decisions behind modern political campaigns.

title: Business Uncovered: How Business Really Works
author: Marcus Bennett
description:
Business Uncovered: How Business Really Works

What really happens behind the businesses, systems, strategies, and decisions that shape the world around us?

Welcome to Business Uncovered, a documentary-style business podcast that explores how businesses actually work beneath the surface.

Every episode takes a closer look at the hidden mechanics of modern business from supply chains and distribution networks to franchising, manufacturing, subscriptions, logistics, retail, technology, pricing structures, marketplaces, customer journeys, business operations, and the systems that allow companies to serve millions of people.

Instead of simply telling the story of a successful company, Business Uncovered asks a different question: What is happening underneath the business?

How does a supermarket make money from thousands of products? Why do airlines operate with such complicated pricing? How can a free product become a billion-dollar business? Why do some companies rely on franchises while others own every location? What makes a business model difficult to copy? And how can a seemingly simple operation become a powerful business system?

Each episode breaks down one fascinating business mechanism, industry practice, or commercial system and explains it through clear storytelling, real-world examples, research, and practical analysis.

You don't need an MBA to understand business.

Business Uncovered turns complicated business concepts into engaging stories that reveal the systems most people never notice.

Whether you're an entrepreneur, business owner, executive, marketer, student, creator, or simply curious about how the commercial world works, this podcast will help you see everyday businesses from a completely different perspective.

No boring lectures. No business jargon for the sake of jargon.

Just fascinating business questions, surprising explanations, and clear insights into the systems behind modern commerce.

Because once you understand how the system works, you start seeing business differently.

Business Uncovered.

How Business Really Works.

title: Storytelling Circles: A story for a story
author: missjae6
description:
Last year, Verna and I joked about starting a podcast where we could record all the things we have to say. At the time, it was a dream rooted in humor—because really, who has the time?

But why a podcast, you ask?

As sisters, Verna and I have always connected through conversation. We have shared life as sisters, mothers, and women, navigating all the joys, challenges, and unexpected adventures that come our way. No matter the distance between us—whether it was when I left for college, when she met her soulmate and got married, when we went from being a ten-minute walk apart to a four-hour drive, and now an entire ocean away—we have always found our way back to each other through storytelling.

We talk almost every day.

You might wonder what we could possibly have left to talk about. The truth is, when it comes to storytelling, the content is endless. There is always a new memory to revisit, a lesson to unpack, a moment to celebrate, or something hilarious to laugh about. And let's be honest—there is always something to laugh about.

So here we are, finally bringing that dream to life and creating a space where we can do what we love most: talk story.

This fall, we'll launch our inaugural podcast, Storytelling Circles: A Story for a Story. Each episode will be an invitation into our circle as we share stories, reflections, laughter, and conversations that connect us across the ocean. We'll also welcome guests to join us, bringing their own stories and experiences to the circle.

We invite you to listen in, where every story finds a place in an unending circle—and where two sisters, separated by an ocean, stay connected through storytelling, laughter, and the simple joy of sharing life together.

Now, a small disclaimer: we are novice podcasters and completely inexperienced behind the microphone. But when it comes to storytelling? We're seasoned sisters with a lifetime of practice.

We hope you'll join our circle.

Hosted by Kirsten and Jeanne, business owners who have been outsourcing for more than 19 years across five countries, this podcast goes far beyond simply hiring a virtual assistant.
You'll learn how to hire, manage, delegate to, and leverage virtual assistants, build systems and SOPs, use AI and automation, and determine what work you should actually keep on your plate.
We'll share the lessons we've learned from years of hiring virtual assistants and working with international virtual teams, including what works, what doesn't, the mistakes we've made, and what we wish every business owner knew before hiring their first VA.
We'll talk about:
- How to find and hire the right virtual assistant

description:
Alexander the Great by Jacob Abbott.  
"Alexander the Great" by Jacob Abbott is a historical account written in the late 19th century. The book chronicles the life and exploits of one of history's most famous military leaders, Alexander the Great, focusing on his childhood, education, and the early part of his reign. With a detailed exploration of Alexander's character, ambitions, and the political landscape of the time, the narrative sets the stage for the broader themes of conquest and leadership that will unfold throughout the text. The opening of the book introduces the reader to Alexander's formative years, highlighting his remarkable lineage as the son of King Philip of Macedon and Queen Olympias. It describes his upbringing, education under great thinkers like Aristotle, and the early signs of his extraordinary capabilities and impetuous nature. Key anecdotes, such as his legendary connection with his warhorse Bucephalus, illustrate both his mental acuity and physical prowess. As the narrative unfolds, it captures the tension between his noble character and the brutal realities of the ambitious world he inhabits, hinting at the greatness that is to come as he navigates the complex dynamics of his family and the larger political landscape.

Parenting a child with autism comes with a lot of questions. Does speech therapy really help? What about ABA therapy? How do you travel with an autistic child, survive restaurants, train a service dog, find the right providers, and figure out whether something is autism... or just plain old orneryism?


Welcome to Autism Rewritten, where Carrie “The Mom” shares what life is really like raising her autistic daughter, and Helen “The Aunt” asks a lot of questions. Sometimes very basic questions. 


Carrie talks openly about what's worked for their family, what hasn't, the therapies they've tried, the things they've done differently, and the things they've learned along the way. We'll chat about nonverbal autism, speech therapy, occupational therapy, ABA therapy, service dogs, traveling with an autistic child, everyday family life, adventures, and those moments nobody prepares you for.


No two autistic children are the same, and this isn't a podcast about telling you how to raise yours. It's one mom's experience raising one pretty amazing kid, with an aunt along for the ride who is perfectly willing to ask, "Wait... what does that mean?"


There will be opinions. There will be questions. There will probably be '80s and '90s references. And occasionally we'll wonder why we thought adding a podcast to our busy lives was a good idea.


This is autism in real life. The hard parts, the funny parts, the things that worked, the things that absolutely did not, and the wins worth celebrating.

author: Rachel Fitzpatrick
description:
**You can lead a team, manage a career, solve everyone else’s problems—and still completely lose trust in yourself when someone you love is unhappy with you.**

I’m Rachel Fitzpatrick, certified Project Management Professional and yoga teacher, and I’ll show you how to stop managing your partner’s emotions, set boundaries without guilt, and trust your own judgment—**so you can stop constantly wondering if you’re the problem and confidently lead your romantic life like you lead your career.**
Because this isn't just about getting better at boundaries. It's about being able to say what you mean, make your own decisions, and stand by what you know—even when your partner is unhappy with you. Without needing your friends, your therapist, Google, or your partner to confirm that what you feel is reasonable. **Without making someone else’s reaction the price of admission for trusting yourself.**
Each week, we **squeeze** one of the painful, confusing parts of relationships that can make even the most capable woman question herself:
*Am I asking for too much?*
*Was that boundary selfish?*
*Should I apologize?*
*Am I communicating my pain—or punishing my partner?*
*Is this actually a problem, or am I the problem?*
Then we get to the **juice**: what’s really happening underneath the pattern, why you keep getting pulled into it, and what you can actually do differently.
Through self-leadership, project management methodology, and yoga, you'll learn how to turn insight into action—and action into evidence.
Every episode leaves you with a **Microdose of Courage**: one small action to practice choosing yourself even when someone you love doesn't like it.
Because the goal isn't to become better at managing your relationship.
**It's to become a woman who trusts herself enough to decide how she wants to participate in it.**
You are your most important project.

title: The Quiet Cost
author: Tiffany Howe
description:
From the outside, everything looks like it's working. You're successful. You're capable. You're the one people count on.

But underneath, something is shifting. The roles keep multiplying. The praise keeps coming. You keep holding it all together — and somewhere along the way, you've started to feel like a stranger in your own life.

People call it burnout. And it does look like burnout — the exhaustion, the depletion, the sense that something is off. But burnout is just a symptom. Not the source. What's really happening is quieter and harder to name: the over-functioning that gets called dedication. The invisible labor that gets called being responsible. The mental load that gets called what you're good at. The self-abandonment that gets called maturity. The identity erosion that no one sees — because you're still smiling, still delivering, still holding it all together.

The Quiet Cost is a podcast for high-achieving, capable women navigating what hides underneath the systems they're praised for holding together. The careers. The families. The faith communities. The advocacy work. The mental load nobody else sees. You're not collapsing. You're not falling apart. You're just slowly, steadily, shrinking yourself to keep everything else functioning.

And here's what no one is saying out loud: the problem usually isn't how much you're carrying. It's that what actually matters to you and how you're living have started to drift apart. You can't rest your way out of that. You can't boundary your way out of it. That drift is what you've been feeling all along — and what you haven't been able to name.

Hosted by leadership coach Tiffany Howe, each episode meets you where you are: still functioning, still capable, and quietly becoming someone you don't recognize. Together we'll explore what it costs to keep performing inside systems that reward your shrinking, and what it looks like to come back to the version of yourself you've been overriding — across every role you carry.

For the women who've tried the productivity tips, the boundaries, the self-care, and the rest — and are starting to suspect the problem isn't what they're doing.

It's what it's been costing them to keep doing it.

Welcome to The Quiet Cost.

title: The Unfinished Church
author: Wesleyan Impact Partners
description:
The church's work is not done, and the Holy Spirit is never done with us.
The Unfinished Church is a podcast about the church still on its way: going on to perfection, as the Wesleyan tradition puts it, not as a claim of arrival but as a prayer and a posture. Each season, Host Bishop Gregory Vaughn Palmer sits down with leaders, scholars, and practitioners from across the church for honest conversations about what it looks like to follow the Spirit to the edges, where the church is most visibly unfinished and most urgently needed.
This series traces a single question: what does it mean to be a church that is still becoming? Palmer's guests bring that question to life from radically different vantage points. A historian who reads the Methodist past as spiritual formation. The president of the only historically Black seminary in the UMC. A theologian who leads a seminary from the margins inward, having planted a Hispanic church in Eastern Durham and started a course of study for ministers in El Salvador. A bishop building full communion across denominational lines while opening a sanctuary to every Abrahamic faith in her city. A layperson doing justice work in prisons and insisting the church cannot export its calling. A pastor who found the unfinished church in a congregation of fewer than fifty people and never looked back.
Together they challenge the metrics the church has used to measure itself and ask a harder question: not how do we finish the church, but how do we change what we think finishing looks like?
This is a show for people who love the church enough to tell the truth about it and hopeful enough to keep working. Whether you lead a congregation, serve a denomination, or simply feel called to be bound to others in the human family, you are welcome here.
The Unfinished Church is produced by Wesleyan Impact Partners and Texas Methodist Foundation. New episodes wherever you listen to podcasts.

Her Health, Her Way – A Podcast for Women Who Want to Take Charge of Their Wellness


Jen Kruba-Couch, a dōTERRA essential oils expert with a deep passion for holistic health, brings you Her Health, Her Way—your go-to podcast for all things female wellness. But this isn’t just about essential oils—Jen lives and breathes the lifestyle she shares, offering expert insights on natural health, nutrition, self-care, and more.

title: Operation Truth
author: Lou Palumbo and Tom Fuentes
description:
I'm Lou Palumbo. I spent 53 years in law enforcement and a lot of years traveling, listening, and learning from people smarter than me.

This show is called Operation Truth because that's the whole idea. No agenda. Nobody paying me to say anything. I'm not here to tell you who to vote for or how to think. I'm here to give you food for thought.

Every week I take on the things this country can't seem to talk about without going at each other's throats. Guns. Immigration. The media. The technology watching all of us. I'll tell you what I've seen firsthand, I'll tell you when I don't know something, and I'll ask you to fact check me.

But I'm going to ask you for three things while we do this. Civility. Decency. Respect. Those left the conversation somewhere along the way, and I think that costs us more than any single issue does.

Mostly, this show is about our children. My generation broke a lot of what they were supposed to believe in. The least we can do now is be honest with them.

You don't have to agree with me. I'll still be your friend.

He has sat across the table from founders during the deals that made them and the moments that almost broke them.
Bronx CFO: Street to Suite is where the guard comes down. Founders and family business owners sit across from Simon and talk about the money, the risks, and the decisions nobody sees from the outside.

title: Disability Heroes
author: Chronicle
description:
Every disability law practice starts with a story. A career that fell apart. A client who changed everything. A case that hit too close to home.

Disability Heroes is a conversation series about the people behind Social Security disability law: who they are, how they fight for their clients, and what they have learned building a practice that works. One guest, one practice, and an unhurried conversation that covers the personal side and the business side in equal measure.

Most guests represent SSDI and SSI claimants through applications, appeals, and ALJ hearings. Some are disability attorneys. Some are EDPNAs and other non-attorney representatives. All of them do difficult, largely invisible work, and this show exists to put it on the record under their own names.

Episodes get into the craft and the operations together: hearing preparation and what actually moves an administrative law judge, gathering and organizing medical evidence, keeping clients steady through waits measured in years, continuing disability reviews and overpayment notices, and the economics of a contingency practice. Expect the intake decisions that shape a caseload, hiring and training the first few employees, and what technology has genuinely changed about disability law firm operations versus what it has only promised. Guests disagree with each other on plenty of it, and those disagreements are left in.

Episodes run about thirty to sixty minutes, with guests from solo practices to national firms. Hosted by Will Yang and produced by Chronicle.

title: Business on the Run

title: The Great Repair
author: ETC
description:
Após ter viajado por Berlim (2023) e Paris (2024), a exposição The Great Repair chega a Nairobi em julho de 2026, num formato enriquecido e com curadoria de Munyu, um coletivo de artistas quenianos.

Esta exposição de arquitetura explora os desafios ecológicos e éticos do nosso tempo, abordando questões de cuidado, reparação, manutenção e transformação do ambiente construído na era do colapso ecológico.

Através do trabalho de diversos arquitetos e estúdios de todo o mundo, a exposição destaca práticas e narrativas que funcionam como contraponto aos modelos extrativistas e orientados para o consumo - abordando questões como a degradação ambiental, o esgotamento de recursos e as desigualdades socioespaciais, muitas das quais enraízadas em legados coloniais.

Em paralelo com a exposição, e em colaboração com a equipa curatorial do Munyu, Eléonore Labattut (ETC) está a desenvolver uma série de podcasts concebida como uma extensão contextual destes temáticas. O objetivo é ampliar a investigação da exposição sobre reparação ecológica, práticas de cuidado, reutilização de materiais e justiça ambiental, situando estas questões nas condições espaciais, sociais e climáticas específicas do Quénia. A série será composta por seis episódios, com as vozes de arquitetos, ativistas e investigadoras que, através da diversidade das suas práticas e perspetivas, irão abranger, ampliar e contextualizar o vasto leque de questões levantadas pela exposição. 

__

After touring Berlin (2023) and Paris (2024), the exhibition The Great Repair arrives in Nairobi in July 2026, in an expanded format curated by Munyu, a collective of Kenyan artists.

This architecture exhibition explores the ecological and ethical challenges of our time, addressing issues of care, repair, maintenance, and transformation of the built environment in the era of ecological collapse.
Through the work of various architects and studios from around the world, the exhibition highlights practices and narratives that serve as a counterpoint to extractivist and consumption-oriented models - addressing issues such as environmental degradation, resource depletion, and socio-spatial inequalities, many of which are rooted in colonial legacies.

In parallel with the exhibition, and in collaboration with the Munyu curatorial team, Eléonore Labattut (ETC) is developing a podcast series conceived as a contextual extension of these themes. The goal is to expand the exhibition’s exploration of ecological restoration, care practices, material reuse, and environmental justice, situating these issues within the specific spatial, social, and climatic conditions of Kenya. The series will consist of six episodes, featuring the voices of architects, activists, and researchers who, through the diversity of their practices and perspectives, will explore, expand upon, and contextualize the wide range of issues raised by the exhibition.

The recollections of the experiences of 3 women who had early stage (stage 1 or 2) breast cancer. Between the 3 of them, they have, or had, 4 breasts affected.
They share their experiences navigating the whole experience from diagnosis, through treatment and to life after cancer. You’ll hear about the various treatments - chemotherapy, surgery, reconstruction, radiotherapy and hormone therapy.

Most mental health podcasts sound like a gentle hug. This one sounds like a reality check from your funniest friend who is also barely holding it together.
Welcome to The Dopamine Dealer, where we explore the chaotic intersection of mental health, anxiety, and the kind of dark humor you usually save for your therapist. We aren’t here to fix you (because we aren’t doctors), but we are here to make you laugh at the things that usually make you cry.

At 46, a late autism and ADHD diagnosis has helped me understand just how important joy and dopamine are in my life. This podcast explores the hobbies, passions, adventures, and everyday moments that make life brighter and more interesting.
Through personal stories and conversations with guests, I'll uncover what people chase for their dopamine fix and why it means so much to them. Expect inspiration, honesty, laughter, and plenty of ideas for bringing more joy into your own life.

Welcome to your Bridal Era.
Planning a wedding is wonderful, but it can also be completely overwhelming. I'm Georgie Le Roux, founder of the Bridal brand Gigi & Olive. Every week I sit down with the planners, designers and real Brides I have spent years learning from, and ask them all the things you actually want to know. From cult classics and childhood favourites to absolute cinematic disasters, each episode dives deep into why these films mean so much to the people who love them (even if no one else does). 🎧 New episodes every week on all podcast platforms. 🎥 Video versions, bonus episodes, and more are available on Patreon. patreon.com/everyonesacriticpod

title: رادیو ماشینی
author: Mehrdad Naeimi
description:
به «رادیو ماشینی» خوش آمدید؛ جایی که مرز بین انسان و ماشین کم‌رنگ‌تر از همیشه شده است.
*رادیو ماشینی* یک پادکست فارسی درباره جهانی است که آرام‌آرام دارد ماشینی می‌شود.
اینجا درباره چیزهایی حرف می‌زنیم که جهان امروز را ساخته‌اند و چیزهایی که ممکن است جهان فردا را بسازند؛ از *هوش مصنوعی و تکنولوژی، علم و آینده، تاریخ و جامعه، اقتصاد و سیاست، فلسفه و روان‌شناسی* گرفته تا ایده‌ها، اختراعات، اتفاق‌ها و آدم‌هایی که مسیر زندگی انسان را تغییر داده‌اند.
رادیو ماشینی با کمک *هوش مصنوعی* ساخته می‌شود؛ از پژوهش و پردازش اطلاعات تا بخش‌هایی از تولید و روایت. اما موضوع اصلی ما خودِ هوش مصنوعی نیست. سؤال بزرگ‌تر این است:
*وقتی جهان ما هر روز بیشتر شبیه یک ماشین می‌شود، خودِ انسان قرار است چه شکلی شود؟*
در هر قسمت سراغ یک داستان، پرونده، پرسش یا پدیده می‌رویم و تلاش می‌کنیم پشت روایت‌های آشنا را ببینیم؛ اینکه چرا اتفاقی افتاد، چه چیزی را تغییر داد و چه ارتباطی با دنیایی دارد که امروز در آن زندگی می‌کنیم.
اگر به *پادکست‌های فارسی، داستان‌های واقعی، تاریخ، علم، فناوری، هوش مصنوعی، فلسفه، روان‌شناسی، جامعه‌شناسی، آینده‌پژوهی، تکنولوژی و پرسش‌های عجیب درباره جهان* علاقه دارید، به رادیو ماشینی خوش آمدید.
*رادیو ماشینی؛ صدای جهانی که دارد ماشین می‌شود.*

title: Specificity Matters
author: specificitymatters
description:
Specificity Matters is the official podcast of the Gonstead Clinical Studies Society’s College of Fellows.  Hosted by Dr David A. Fowler, DC, FGCSS, the show gives the profession’s most rigorously credentialed Gonstead practitioners a public voice - defending the traditional concepts of Clarence Gonstead while examining them in the light of current scientific and philosophical thought.  
Each episode explores the foundations of the Gonstead method:  specific analysis, the disc as the primary lesion, and the irreplaceable art of the hands-on adjustment.  Fellows name their sources, argue their positions, and take seriously the question every clinician should ask - does the evidence hold?
For chiropractors, students, and anyone who believes a tradition worth preserving is one that can withstand honest scrutiny, this is your seat at the table.

title: WineSoul
author: Wine Soul
description:
Wine Soul is a podcast about two childhood friends who became adults—in theory.
Now dads and quintessential millennials, they're still as geeky, passionate, and ridiculous as they were as teenagers. The only difference is they're now bourgeois enough to obsess over wine with the same unhealthy confidence they once brought to arguments about things that never mattered.
They explore wine, history, nostalgia, and travel through thirty years of friendship, relentless curiosity, and a generous amount of humour.
Wine Soul is good wine, the occasional moment of substance, and a lot of laughs—brought to you by two old friends who never take themselves too seriously.
Their taste matured. They didn't.

title: Art Saves Lives
author: Stacey Chillemi
description:
Brett Ashby paints portraits while riding a skateboard, live, in front of crowds, on three continents.

Award-winning contemporary artist, cancer survivor, and speaker, Ashby has spent more than twenty years turning movement, fear, and lived experience into art, with subjects ranging from Barack Obama to Princess Diana and an audience of over 130,000. This series is for anyone carrying something heavy and looking for somewhere to put it. Creativity as a lifeline. Movement as therapy. Survival as purpose. Follow the series.

title: RATCHET-UP with Allan Breidenbach

description:
RATCHET-UP with Allan Breidenbach is a leadership podcast for executives, managers, and business owners who need to drive change without losing their people.

Most companies focus on process, and that’s where things break.

In this show, Allan Breidenbach, president and general manager of Wick Buildings and creator of the RATCHET-UP system, shares a practical, people-first approach to change management. Through conversations with leaders and executives across industries, each episode breaks down real-world leadership challenges and shows how to build readiness, create alignment, earn trust, communicate with clarity, and keep teams engaged through change.

You will learn how to lead organizational change with less resistance, strengthen team alignment, improve productivity and operational efficiency, avoid common leadership mistakes that slow progress, and turn change into measurable profit and performance.

If you lead a team, run a business, or manage operations, this podcast shows you how to stop forcing change and start leading it in a way people will follow.

title: Pets and People
author: Connor Borowski and Payal Samuel
description: Welcome to Pets & People — the podcast where animal and human health come together. Hosted by a veterinarian and a chiropractor, we share practical advice, real stories, and expert insight on caring for your pets and your own body. From mobility and injuries to wellness, prevention, and everyday health tips, we help you better understand the connection between pets, people, and living healthier together.

title: The Story Stays
author: Tina Konstant
description:
Welcome to The Story Stays
Previously Waffle-Free Storytelling (then StoryRiverFables for a while). I'm like a chameleon in a paintbox... can't quite make up my mind. The name has changed, but the vibe hasn't. This show is all story... no waffle. The original name came about while I was looking for a story show, and all I could find at the time were shows that had a story... but you had to wade through minutes and minutes of jibber-fabber! "Enough of the waffle!!" I yelled to the four walls... and Waffle-Free Storytelling was born.
NO WAFFLE! No rambling introduction, no jibber-jabber. A waffle-free story still gets straight to the point: story and nothing but. What you take from it is all yours.
The tales are 3 to 17 minutes long and, except for a few traditional stories or ones delivered by one of my amazing guests, are written and told by yours truly (Tina Konstant).
The tales are all fable’ish, myth’ish, fairytale’ish, and entirely human (zero AI... I repeat - NO A.I.).
Welcome to the place where coffee breaks become mini adventures, headphones become front-row seats, and truth is told through stories.
See you on the flipside, you wild, glorious human being.
Tina

title: 世界經典名著有聲書~小王子英文版
author: Vincent Lee
description:
《小王子》是法國貴族作家、詩人、飛行員先驅安東尼·德·聖修伯里創作的最著名的小說，發表於1943年。作為法語書籍中擁有最多讀者和譯本的小說，《小王子》曾當選為20世紀法國最佳圖書。它是世界最暢銷的圖書之一，被翻譯成250多種語言和方言，全世界迄今已售出兩億多冊，年銷售一百多萬冊。
 
本專輯是經典名著，小王子的中英文朗讀版。
不僅是適合小孩子，也適合大人閱讀的一本故事書。歡迎喜愛英文，喜愛朗讀的朋友們一起交流學習。

From discussing the benefits of mindfulness and meditation to exploring the joys of hobbies and creative pursuits, we'll cover a wide range of topics aimed at helping you cultivate a more balanced and fulfilling lifestyle. You'll hear from experts, enthusiasts, and everyday individuals who have discovered the transformative power of embracing leisure in their lives.


Whether you're listening during your morning commute, while taking a leisurely walk, or as you unwind after a long day, each episode of the Unwind and Enjoy Podcast is designed to leave you feeling inspired, refreshed, and ready to embrace the beauty of life's simplest pleasures.


So grab your favorite beverage, find a cozy spot to relax, and join us as we embark on this journey of self-discovery, relaxation, and joy. Welcome to the Unwind and Enjoy Podcast—where leisure meets inspiration.

author: April DJ Snow
description:
Welcome to Created by God to Be…
I’m April Snow. Together, we’ll explore Scripture, faith, identity, belonging, and what it means to become the person God created each of us to be.
